compareCandidate.label: Seed vs. spore
compareCandidate.description: A seed holds a baby plant (embryo) plus stored food inside a protective coat. A spore is tiny and has no stored food; it is a simpler way some plants reproduce.

processes: Germination - seed sprouting into a new plant
Storing the baby plant's first food
plainLanguageExplanation: A seed is a baby plant in a box. It has a hard outer coat that protects it, a tiny embryo that is the actual baby plant, and stored food the baby plant can use to get started. When a seed lands in the right place - with some water, warmth, and air - it germinates: it takes in water, the embryo begins to grow, and a tiny root and shoot push out. Later it becomes a new plant. Seeds can be carried by wind, water, and animals to new places.

whyItMatters: Seeds are how flowering plants make the next generation and spread over the land. Understanding seeds explains how new plants grow, how farmers plant crops, and why animals (including us) eat things like whole grains and nuts.
tagline: A baby plant in a box
didYouKnow: Some seeds are spread far by the wind, others by water or by animals eating fruit and carrying the seeds to new places.
